<div style="border:1px solid #303030; border-radius:4px; padding:16px 20px;">

== Grammar bot configuration ==

These settings control the '''Grammar bot''' run by [[User:StubManager|StubManager]]. Only edits by sysops, bureaucrats and the wiki owner are used; any other edit is ignored and reverted automatically. Results are published at [[User:StubManager/Reports/Grammar]].

'''Priority of settings:''' Wiki (this page) > Secrets (GitHub) > Defaults (in the code). A value that is left empty is treated as "not set".

=== Settings ===
Change the value after the <code>=</code> and save. Lines starting with <code>#</code> are comments.

<pre class="grammar-settings">
# Master switch for the Grammar bot. false = nothing runs (reports are not updated, nothing is edited).
enabled = true

# report = only write the report pages. preview = also show exactly which edits WOULD be made. apply = really make the approved edits.
mode = report

# Which rules run. 'all' or a comma-separated list of rule IDs (see the rule pages).
rules_enabled = all

# Rules an admin has approved for automatic fixing. Empty = nothing is ever edited. A rule also needs enough review evidence (see below).
autofix_rules = 

# How many findings of a rule must have been spot-checked by a human before it may be automatic.
autofix_min_reviewed = 50

# Minimum percentage of those spot-checked findings that were correct (for example 98).
autofix_min_precision = 98

# Safety cap: the most pages the bot will edit in one run. 0 = no edits at all.
max_edits_per_run = 20

# If a page needs more automatic fixes than this, the bot leaves it for a human (very messy pages are risky).
max_fixes_per_page = 15

# The bot will not edit a page that someone changed within this many hours (avoids fighting an editor who is mid-way through a rewrite).
min_page_age_hours = 24

# Pause between edits in milliseconds (keeps the bot polite and rate-limit safe).
edit_interval_ms = 2500

# true = text inside "quotation marks" is never changed or flagged (dialogue is often written in an unusual style).
skip_quotes = true

# Pages in these categories are not checked at all.
exempt_categories = Typo exempt,Googology,Salad numbers,Stub exempt

# Page titles that are not checked (comma-separated).
exempt_titles = main page

# Optional regular expression; matching page titles are not checked. Empty = none.
exempt_title_regex = 

# Only check this many pages (for testing). 0 = every page.
max_pages = 0

# Where the report pages are saved. Sub-pages are created below this title.
reports_base = User:StubManager/Reports/Grammar

# Most findings listed on each rule page (the counts are always complete).
report_rows_per_rule = 400

# Most findings listed per article on each rule page, so one messy page cannot fill the list.
report_max_per_page_per_rule = 5

# How many pages the "Worst pages" report lists.
report_worst_pages = 300

# Size of the random spot-check sample on each rule page.
report_sample_size = 25

# Rare-word rule: a word counts as rare if it appears at most this many times on the whole wiki.
freq_rare_max = 2

# Rare-word rule: the similar word must appear at least this many times.
freq_common_min = 30

# Rare-word rule: the similar word must be at least this many times more frequent than the rare word.
freq_ratio_min = 10

# Rare-word rule: ignore words shorter than this.
freq_min_length = 5

# Rare-word rule: most suggestions listed.
freq_max_rows = 300
</pre>

=== Ignore list ===
Words or phrases the bot must never flag (invented names, deliberate spellings). One per line or comma-separated. A phrase containing spaces ignores any finding whose surroundings contain it.

<pre class="grammar-ignore">
# example: Voidance, Omniverse
</pre>

=== Extra misspellings ===
One per line as <code>wrong -> right</code>. These are added to the built-in list.

<pre class="grammar-misspellings">
# example: omniverce -> omniverse
</pre>

=== Reviews (evidence for automatic fixing) ===
After spot-checking a rule's sample, record <code>rule_id@version = checked, wrong</code>. The version must match the rule's current version or the review is treated as outdated.

<pre class="grammar-reviews">
# example: known_misspelling@1 = 50, 1
</pre>

=== Word lists ===
These lists '''extend''' the built-in lists. Start a line with <code>-</code> to remove a built-in entry (for example <code>-this</code>).

'''Connecting words''' (wrongly capitalised after a comma):
<pre class="grammar-glue">
# example: whereupon
</pre>

'''Abbreviations''' (a full stop after these does not end a sentence; no dot at the end):
<pre class="grammar-abbreviations">
# example: gov
</pre>

'''Words that may be repeated''' (for example "had had"):
<pre class="grammar-repeat-ok">
# example: bis
</pre>

'''Names that start with a lowercase letter on purpose''':
<pre class="grammar-lowercase-names">
# example: iphone
</pre>

=== Rollout guide ===
# '''Report phase:''' leave <code>mode = report</code> and <code>autofix_rules</code> empty. Read the reports, fix false positives with the lists above.
# '''Review phase:''' spot-check each rule's sample and record the result in the reviews box.
# '''Preview phase:''' add trusted rules to <code>autofix_rules</code>, set <code>mode = preview</code> and read the Planned fixes page.
# '''Apply phase:''' set <code>mode = apply</code>. Keep <code>max_edits_per_run</code> small at first.
# '''Emergency stop:''' <code>enabled = false</code>.

</div>
